title: vehicle and air brake pre-trip inspections
objectives: Explain the importance of conducting a pre-trip inspection and who is responsible for it
State which vehicles require daily written inspection reports and what every report must include
Explain how to perform an air brake system inspection, including all key pressure values
List the steps of a pre-trip inspection: under hood, in cab, circle checks and brake tests
Identify the time limits for completing the pre-trip inspection for each licence class
State when pre-hill, en route and post-trip inspections are required and what to check

sections.title: Driver responsibility and NSC trip-inspection rules
points: You must determine your vehicle is in safe operating condition before you drive it — every time.
NSC vehicles must be inspected before use each day (pre-trip) and after the final trip (post-trip).
The driver or another person specified by the carrier inspects; driver and carrier share responsibility.
Written daily reports: buses seating more than 10 including driver, heavy two-axle trucks, trucks towing heavy trailers.
Every report lists plate/unit numbers, all defects (or states none found), date and inspector's signature.
If you couple to another trailer, obtain and carry that trailer's trip inspection report for the day.
With co-drivers, one signature is enough if all agree; if they disagree, all must sign and note it.
mustKnow: Written reports required for a bus, school bus, special activity bus, special vehicle or limousine with a seating capacity of more than 10 including the driver
Written reports required for a two-axle truck or truck-tractor with a licensed GVW greater than 14,600 kg
Written reports required for a truck or truck-tractor towing a trailer that has a licensed GVW greater than 8,200 kg
All trip inspection reports must be given to the carrier within 20 days

check.q: Within how many days must trip inspection reports be given to the carrier?
check.explanation: The manual states all trip inspection reports must be given to the carrier within 20 days.

check.q: A two-axle truck needs a daily written inspection report when its licensed GVW is greater than:
check.explanation: Two-axle trucks or truck-tractors with a licensed GVW greater than 14,600 kg require daily written reports.

sections.title: Cargo securement and re-inspection intervals
points: Under the NSC, every vehicle transporting cargo on a highway must be inspected for cargo securement, regardless of weight.
Before driving, confirm operating equipment (tailgate, doors, tarpaulins, spare tire) is secured.
Ensure cargo doesn't interfere with safe operation of the vehicle or with exiting it.
Re-inspect the cargo securement system within 80 km of the loading point.
Then re-inspect at the earliest of: a change in duty status, three hours, or 240 km of driving.
Record cargo securement inspections on your daily logs.
No inspection needed if cargo is sealed and you're ordered not to inspect it, or it's inaccessible.
mustKnow: Re-inspect the cargo securement system within 80 km from the point where the cargo was loaded
Re-inspect at the earliest of: a change in duty status of the driver, three hours of driving, or 240 km of driving since the last inspection

check.q: After loading, you must re-inspect the cargo securement system within:
check.explanation: The first cargo re-check must happen within 80 km from the point where the cargo was loaded.

check.q: During the trip, cargo must be re-inspected at the earliest of a duty status change, three hours of driving, or:
check.explanation: The interval is the earliest of a duty status change, three hours, or 240 km since the last inspection.

sections.title: Road-test inspection report and time limits
points: On your road test, the examiner gives you a blank trip inspection report to complete and return.
Part of your grade is based on how completely and accurately you fill out the report.
Corrected defects must be noted with a signature certifying the correction; minor defects noted as not needing immediate repair.
Time limits: Class 1 under 45 minutes; Class 3 under 30 minutes; Class 2 under 30 minutes.
Class 4 unrestricted (bus) under 20 minutes; Class 4 restricted under 15 minutes.
With manual slack adjusters you must adjust a brake; with automatic ones, explain how manual adjustment is done.
During the test, point to or touch items you inspect and tell the examiner what you're looking for.
mustKnow: Class 1 pre-trip inspection: complete in less than 45 minutes
Class 3 pre-trip inspection: complete in less than 30 minutes
Class 2 pre-trip inspection: less than 30 minutes; Class 4 (unrestricted) less than 20 minutes
Class 4 (restricted) pre-trip inspection: complete in less than 15 minutes

check.q: How long do you have to complete a Class 1 tractor-trailer pre-trip inspection on your road test?
check.explanation: The Class 1 pre-trip inspection should be completed in less than 45 minutes.

check.q: If your test vehicle has automatic slack adjusters, you will be asked to:
choices: Adjust the automatic slack adjusters by hand
Explain how to adjust manual slack adjuster brakes
check.explanation: With automatic slack adjusters, you must explain how to adjust manual slack adjuster brakes for proper pushrod travel.

sections.title: Inspection structure: under hood, in cab, circle checks and brake tests
points: Before starting: park on level ground away from traffic, set parking brakes, shut off the engine, block the wheels.
Under hood: check fluids, belts, hoses, compressor, steering components, suspension and frame; drain the supply reservoir.
In cab: check tires/wheels/mud flaps, foundation brakes, gauges, wipers, heater, horns, emergency equipment, seatbelts, mirrors, documents.
Walk the circle check counter-clockwise so you're facing oncoming traffic.
Circle check for lights: turn signals, low and high beams, tail, licence plate, clearance and brake lights.
Finish with tug tests against the parking brakes, then move ahead slowly checking brake response and steering wheel slack.
Follow the same order every time so you don't miss items.
mustKnow: A peace officer may place your vehicle out of service if drum brake linings are less than 1/4 inch (6.4 mm) thick or air disc brake pads are less than 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick

check.q: In which direction should you walk during the circle check?
choices: Counter-clockwise, so you face oncoming traffic
Clockwise, so traffic approaches from behind
check.explanation: Walk counter-clockwise so you're facing oncoming traffic during the circle check.

check.q: A vehicle may be placed out of service if drum brake linings are thinner than:
check.explanation: Drum linings under 1/4 inch (6.4 mm), or disc pads under 1/8 inch (3.2 mm), can put a vehicle out of service.

sections.title: Air brake system test and its numbers
points: Check the compressor stops pumping (cuts out) between 105 and 135 p.s.i.
Pump down to about 80 per cent of maximum; the governor must cut the compressor in before pressure falls below 80 p.s.i.
Pump down farther: low-air warning devices must activate at or above 60 p.s.i.
Class 1: trailer air supply valve must close between 20 and 45 p.s.i.; check trailer brakes applied.
Class 1: disconnect glad hands and confirm no air escapes; also check them during a foot brake application.
Pressure must rebuild from 50 to 90 p.s.i. within three minutes at fast idle.
Full brake application held one minute: air loss max 4 p.s.i./min (Class 1), 6 with two trailers, 3 for a single-unit truck.
mustKnow: Compressor stops pumping between 105 and 135 p.s.i. (724 and 931 kPa)
The governor must cause the compressor to cut in before pressure falls below 80 p.s.i. (552 kPa)
Low-air warning device(s) activate at or above 60 p.s.i. (414 kPa)
Trailer air supply valve closes when the highest reservoir pressure gauge reads between 20 to 45 p.s.i. (138 to 310 kPa)

Air pressure builds from 50 to 90 p.s.i. (345 to 620 kPa) within three minutes at a fast idle (1,000 to 1,200 r.p.m.); full application (90 to 100 p.s.i.) held one minute — air loss not more than 4 p.s.i. (27.6 kPa) per minute, 6 p.s.i. (41.4 kPa) with two trailers, three p.s.i. (20.7 kPa) for a single-unit truck

check.q: The low-air warning device must activate at or above:
check.explanation: Low-air warning devices must activate at or above 60 p.s.i. (414 kPa).

check.q: During the buildup test, air pressure must rise from 50 to 90 p.s.i. within:
check.explanation: Pressure must build from 50 to 90 p.s.i. within three minutes at a fast idle of 1,000 to 1,200 r.p.m.

sections.title: Class differences and ongoing inspections
points: Class 1 adds trailer items: fifth wheel flush to apron, jaws locked on kingpin, landing gear raised, glad hands, trailer tug test and hand-valve check.
Class 3 single-unit: pump below 50 p.s.i., rebuild pressure, release spring parking brakes if they applied.
Class 2/4 bus adds passenger compartment checks: seats, doors, step lights, emergency windows and exits with alarm.
Class 4 restricted adds trunk, spare tire, jack, brake fluid and propane tank checks; no air brake test.
Pre-hill: stop in the pullout, check reservoir pressure, air leaks, glad hands, drum/hub heat and pushrod travel — even with automatic slack adjusters.
En route: walk around counter-clockwise checking tires, wheels, brakes, hubs, coupling, cargo and suspension.
Post-trip: inspect at the end of the final trip and complete a trip inspection report noting any defects.
mustKnow: Commercial trailers with an overall width of 2.05 m or more are required to have reflective markings to the rear and sides
You may be fined for failing to stop to conduct a brake pre-hill inspection

check.q: At a pre-hill brake check, must you check pushrod travel if your vehicle has automatic slack adjusters?
choices: Yes, you must check pushrod travel even with automatic slack adjusters
Only if the low-air warning came on
No, automatic adjusters make it unnecessary
Only on vehicles towing two trailers
check.explanation: The manual states you must check pushrod travel even if equipped with automatic slack adjusters.

check.q: Commercial trailers must have reflective markings to the rear and sides when their overall width is:
check.explanation: Trailers with an overall width of 2.05 m or more require reflective markings to the rear and sides.

summary: You are responsible for confirming your vehicle is safe before every drive; NSC vehicles need daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections.
Written reports must list defects or state none, be signed and dated, and reach the carrier within 20 days.
Know the air numbers: cut-out 105-135 p.s.i., cut-in before 80, warning at 60, trailer valve closes 20-45, buildup 50-90 in three minutes.
Air-loss limits with full application held one minute: 4 p.s.i./min Class 1, 6 with two trailers, 3 for a single-unit truck.
Keep inspecting after departure: cargo within 80 km then every duty change/3 hours/240 km, pre-hill brake checks, en route walkarounds and a post-trip report.
